title: User Research Interview — Onboarding Flow
description: Interview with Maya about first-time onboarding friction.
transcript: 00:03 Sneha Rao: Thanks so much for making time, Maya. Today I'd love to walk through your experience signing up — what happened, where it went well, where it didn't. Sound okay?
00:18 Maya Iyer: Sounds good, happy to help.
00:21 Sneha Rao: Let's start from the very beginning. What brought you to the product in the first place?
00:28 Maya Iyer: My manager asked our team to try it for meeting notes. Honestly, I signed up because I hate writing minutes — I always miss things.
00:40 Sneha Rao: When you say you miss things, can you give me an example?
00:46 Maya Iyer: Last month I was in a 90-minute planning call and I literally took two pages of notes and still forgot who owned which task. Basically the notes were useless by the next morning.
01:02 Sneha Rao: Got it. So what happened when you first opened the app?
01:08 Maya Iyer: So the sign-up itself was fine — Google login, one click. But then, um, I got dropped into this almost empty dashboard with no meetings and no real hint of what to do next.
01:26 Sneha Rao: What did you expect to see?
01:30 Maya Iyer: I guess I expected it to just join my calendar meetings, like automatically? I didn't realize I had to connect my calendar first. The invite step made me want to give up, honestly.
01:46 Sneha Rao: That's really helpful — the invite step. Can you tell me more about what happened there?
01:52 Maya Iyer: It asked me to pick which meetings it should join, but the list only showed three meetings, and none of them were the ones I actually cared about. I kind of guessed and moved on.
02:08 Sneha Rao: And after you picked those, what happened next?

02:13 Maya Iyer: Nothing, for like two days. No meetings got recorded because — I found out later — my team uses Meet links in the body, not calendar invites, if that makes sense. Nobody told me that.
02:31 Sneha Rao: So for two days you thought it was broken? Did you look for help?
02:37 Maya Iyer: I Googled it, found a help article eventually, but the article was about Zoom, not Google Meet. That was frustrating.
02:49 Sneha Rao: Okay, noted. If we could wave a magic wand, what would have made that first week better?

02:57 Maya Iyer: I'd love a checklist, like a little progress thing — connect calendar, join a meeting, see your first summary. Oh, and maybe a sample meeting so I could see what a good transcript looks like before my own meetings showed up.
03:17 Sneha Rao: A sample meeting — interesting. Has anyone else mentioned that?
03:22 Maya Iyer: My teammate Raj asked the same thing in our standup, actually. He wanted to see what the output would look like before trusting it with real calls.
03:36 Sneha Rao: Let's talk about the first time a real meeting did show up. What was that like?

03:44 Maya Iyer: Oh, that was the aha moment, honestly. The summary was scarily good — it caught action items I didn't even remember being assigned. That's when I told my manager we should pay for it.
04:02 Sneha Rao: What specifically in the summary sold you?

04:07 Maya Iyer: The action items section with people's names on each task. And the chapter things — the topics with timestamps. I could jump right to the pricing discussion without scrubbing the whole recording.
04:24 Sneha Rao: If you had to keep exactly one feature, which one?
04:30 Maya Iyer: The action items. Everything else is nice, but the action items are why I don't take notes anymore.
04:40 Sneha Rao: Last couple of questions. How often do you go back to old meetings?
04:46 Maya Iyer: Every Friday, basically, for our team retro. I search for stuff like what did we promise the client last week. That search is clutch.
05:00 Sneha Rao: What would you change about that search, if anything?
05:04 Maya Iyer: Maybe search within a single meeting from the player? I sometimes remember the meeting but not the exact words. But honestly, it's fine.
05:18 Sneha Rao: Great. Any final thoughts before we wrap up?
05:23 Maya Iyer: Just — make the first week less confusing, and this product is basically perfect for people like me. The empty dashboard nearly lost us as customers.
05:37 Sneha Rao: That is gold, thank you Maya. I'll share the takeaways with the team this week. Have a great day!
05:45 Maya Iyer: Thanks, you too!

summary.overview: Research interview with Maya (ops team lead) on first-time onboarding. Sign-up itself was frictionless (Google one-click), but the empty dashboard gave no guidance, the calendar-connect step was undiscoverable, and Google Meet links in the body weren't captured — leaving the user thinking the product was broken for two days. The retention moment was the first real summary (accurate action items with owners and timestamped topics). Requested fixes: an onboarding checklist, a sample meeting, and meeting-scoped search from the player.
notes: Sign-up via Google was one click and painless
Empty dashboard with no meetings and no next-step hints — first friction point
Calendar connection was undiscoverable; user expected auto-join without setup
Google Meet links in the email body weren't captured — product appeared broken for two days
Help article found via Google was Zoom-focused, adding to the confusion
Aha moment: first real summary — action items with owners, topics with timestamps
Weekly habit: searching past meetings every Friday for the team retro
Teammate Raj independently requested a sample meeting to preview output quality
